claims.text: The target material is a polycrystalline bulk FeCoNiCrMn-based high-entropy alloy with a homogeneous microstructure.
The alloy will be irradiated at room temperature with 200 keV He+ ions.
A calibrated irradiation dose can produce uniform defect formation.
The proposed irradiation will generate point defects and small dislocation loops within grain interiors.
The irradiation-induced defects and dislocation loops will be uniformly distributed.
A mild post-irradiation anneal in an inert atmosphere can stabilize the irradiation-induced defect structures.
Irradiation-induced point defects and small dislocation loops act as magnetic domain-wall pinning centers.
Pinning by the irradiation-induced defects obstructs domain-wall motion during magnetization reversal.
Obstructing domain-wall motion will increase the coercive field.
Under identical magnetic-field cycling conditions, the irradiated sample will have a higher coercive field than a matched unirradiated sample.
A dose that is too low may create too few defects to enhance coercivity.
A dose that is too high may cause excessive damage, compromise material integrity, and diminish or reverse the coercivity benefit.
The coercivity benefit is expected to persist under standard magnetic measurement conditions.
